rv.q: Might have made a sharper play, given how plot-driven Kevin Wade’s original screenplay was.
Commercialism has won out over art... the score is really a collection of unmemorable songs.
The play is better for it, adding the kind of camp a Broadway hopeful deserves.
Despite bursts of charm, the show often feels like it never fully ignites.
Despite my reservations, I could see it going to Broadway and even having success as a touring show.
Working Girl: The Musical absolutely has the ingredients to be a Broadway contender... But in its current form, the show feels like exactly what it is: a work in progress.
An undeniably catchy lineup of songs... but the story drags in spots.

cn.t: The musical adaptation shows promise with nostalgic '80s appeal and energetic performances, but critics agree it needs significant refinement and trimming before it's ready for Broadway.
